raw_response:
I'm a 53-year-old woman who's farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. I only finished primary school, so I don't know the fancy words — I know what my neighbors do and I remember what happened on my own fields. My husband works part-time at the brick factory in town, so most days it's just me out there. That means I have to plan carefully, because I can't be everywhere at once.

**Winter wheat:** I plant in early October, right after the maize comes off. I buy the same improved seed from the county store — 30 yuan a mu. Before planting I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu and work it in. Then in March at jointing, if the wheat looks a little yellow, I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. I *never* skip the topdress. Six years ago I tried to save that money and the wheat turned yellow and thin — I lost almost 100 kg per mu. Never again. I irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. The well is ours but the electricity still costs, so I watch the weather. Wheat is our main crop — we need the grain for food and for selling.

**Summer maize:** The window after wheat harvest is always tight — sometimes only three or four days. I hire Old Zhang's tractor to do a quick rotary till and plant fast. I put all the fertilizer in at planting — about 35 kg of compound fertilizer and a bit of urea in the furrow. There's no time to come back for split application. Hybrid seed is 50 yuan a mu, and you can't save it, so I buy new every year. I irrigate twice if the summer is dry, but usually the July rains help.

I do the spraying and most of the work myself, but I hire two days of help each season for harvest and planting. Hiring costs 150 yuan a day now, but my back isn't what it used to be at 53, and with my husband at the factory I need the extra hands. I figure my total costs this year are about 4,800 yuan. That's a big chunk of our savings, but I'd rather spend it than risk a bad year. My husband's factory job helps, but farm income still matters. I also keep some cash in hand for emergencies — two years ago he got sick and the hospital wanted payment upfront. So I'm not buying more fertilizer than usual, even though some neighbors use more. I know what my land can do, and I'd rather be a little safe than sorry.
